section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis Vectors (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Recall that any 3D vector [x, y, z] is a linear combination of basis vectors i, j, k. Introduce the standard basis: i=[1,0,0], j=[0,1,0], k=[0,0,1].
section_1.example: Imagine a 3D unit cube sitting at the origin; its corners define the reach of our basis vectors.

section_2.title: Defining 3D Transformations (0:45-1:45)
section_2.content: A linear transformation is defined by where the basis vectors i, j, and k land. We represent this as a 3x3 matrix where columns are the transformed vectors i', j', and k'.
section_2.example: An animation shows i, j, and k stretching and rotating into new positions while the grid space deforms accordingly.

section_3.title: Core Concept: The Determinant (1:45-3:00)
section_3.content: The determinant of a 3x3 matrix represents the 'scaling factor' of volume. If the volume of a shape changes from V to V', the determinant is V'/V.
section_3.example: A virtual 'Robo-Dog' model is inside a unit cube. As we apply a transformation matrix, the cube (and the dog) stretches; if the determinant is 2, the dog appears twice as large in volume.

section_4.title: Application: Rotation & Shear (3:00-4:15)
section_4.content: Explain that different matrices perform different geometric operations: Rotations (preserving lengths/volumes) vs. Shear (sliding layers) vs. Scaling.
section_4.example: Use a character's arm: A rotation matrix rotates the elbow joint, while a shear matrix mimics the 'squash and stretch' effect used in 3D animation to express motion.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
section_5.content: Recap: Any 3D linear transformation is simply a remapping of the 3D grid. The 3x3 matrix is the 'recipe' for where the foundation vectors end up.
section_5.example: A quick montage: A complex 3D character mesh transforming through a sequence of matrix multiplications, showcasing the final smooth motion.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
